cards.title: What is AI?
cards.text: Artificial intelligence is software that learns patterns from data to do tasks like translating, recommending or recognising images.

qs.q: AI learns by finding patterns in…

cards.title: Uses of AI
cards.text: AI helps in medicine, farming, traffic, translation and customer help. It saves time but needs human oversight.

cards.title: AI job worries
cards.text: AI may automate some jobs but also create new ones. Learning new skills is the best protection.

qs.q: The best response to job automation is…

cards.title: AI bias
cards.text: If AI learns from biased data, it can treat people unfairly. Diverse data and checking reduce this.

qs.q: AI becomes biased when it learns from…

cards.title: Internet benefits
cards.text: The internet gives instant knowledge, connects people and opens markets. It also brings distraction and risks.

qs.q: A big benefit of the internet is…

cards.title: Digital divide
cards.text: The digital divide is the gap between those who have internet and devices and those who don’t.

qs.q: The digital divide is a gap in…

cards.title: Social media good and bad
cards.text: Social media connects people and spreads ideas, but can cause comparison, addiction and fake news.

qs.q: A risk of social media is…

cards.title: Screen time
cards.text: Too much screen time hurts sleep, focus and eyes. Breaks and limits help.

cards.title: Online privacy
cards.text: Your data has value. Use strong passwords and think before sharing personal details.

cards.title: Cyber crime
cards.text: Phishing, scams and hacking steal money and data. Never share OTPs or click unknown links.

cards.title: Digital payments
cards.text: UPI lets people pay instantly with a phone. It makes payments quick and cuts cash use.

cards.title: Cyberbullying
cards.text: Bullying online can hurt as much as in person. Block, report and tell a trusted adult.

qs.q: If you face cyberbullying, you should…

cards.title: Scientific method
cards.text: Scientists ask a question, test it with experiments and change ideas when evidence says so.

cards.title: Why space research?
cards.text: Space research gives weather forecasts, GPS, communication and new materials, not just discoveries.

qs.q: A daily benefit of space technology is…

cards.title: Satellites
cards.text: Satellites help with communication, navigation, weather and mapping. Farmers and fishers use their data.

cards.title: Renewable innovation
cards.text: Solar, wind and batteries are getting cheaper and are key to cutting pollution.

qs.q: Which is a clean energy source?

cards.title: Vaccines
cards.text: Vaccines train the body to fight a disease before it strikes. They have saved millions of lives.

cards.title: Robotics
cards.text: Robots do dangerous, repetitive or precise work, like in factories and surgery.

cards.title: Curiosity matters
cards.text: Most big inventions began as simple curiosity and many failed attempts.

cards.title: Science and values
cards.text: Science tells us what we can do. Ethics helps us decide what we should do.

cards.title: Climate science
cards.text: Scientists use temperature data and models to understand warming and predict its effects.

cards.title: Gene editing
cards.text: Gene editing can fix some diseases but raises questions about fairness and safety.

cards.title: Science in daily life
cards.text: Refrigerators, phones, medicines and bridges all come from science. It shapes ordinary days.

qs.q: Daily life depends on science because…

cards.title: Importance of scientific temper
cards.text: Scientific temper means asking questions, testing claims and avoiding superstition.

cards.title: Technology: boon or bane
cards.text: Technology can help or harm depending on how we use it. Medicine saves lives; misuse spreads fear.

cards.title: Nuclear energy: pros
cards.text: Nuclear plants produce huge power with very little air pollution or carbon.

qs.q: A benefit of nuclear energy is…

cards.title: Nuclear energy: cons
cards.text: Nuclear waste stays dangerous for ages and accidents can be disastrous, so safety is critical.

qs.q: A danger of nuclear energy is…

cards.title: E-waste
cards.text: Old phones and computers contain toxic metals. Recycle them properly instead of throwing them away.

cards.title: Automation
cards.text: Machines raise speed and quality but may replace some workers. Reskilling is vital.

cards.title: Deepfakes
cards.text: Deepfakes are fake but realistic videos made by AI. They can spread lies, so verify before believing.

cards.title: Tech and health
cards.text: Fitness apps and telemedicine help health, but too much gadget use harms posture and sleep.

cards.title: Responsible innovation
cards.text: Good innovation asks: who benefits, who might be harmed and is it fair to all?

options: Who benefits and who is harmed

cards.title: Tech for the poor
cards.text: Mobile phones help farmers check prices and weather. Technology should reach the poorest too.

cards.title: Online addiction
cards.text: Games and feeds are designed to keep you hooked. Setting limits keeps you in charge.

cards.title: Surveillance
cards.text: Cameras and data tracking can improve safety but may threaten privacy if misused.

cards.title: Pros and cons of automation
cards.text: Self-driving cars could cut accidents but raise questions about jobs and responsibility.

qs.q: A concern about self-driving cars is…
options: Who is responsible in an accident
